problem_statement: The socket API has no helper that reliably transmits an entire buffer to a connected stream (TCP) peer. zsock_send()/zsock_sendmsg() may return after transferring only part of the data, forcing callers to loop themselves. Add helpers that send all requested data and block (up to a caller-supplied timeout) until everything is sent or an error/timeout occurs: one taking a plain buffer, one taking a net_msghdr. Each helper reports the number of bytes actually sent through an output pointer (which may be NULL), resets it to 0, returns 0 on full success, -ETIMEDOUT if the timeout elapses, -errno on other failures. The helpers are only valid for stream sockets; calling them on a non-stream socket (e.g. UDP) must fail with -EOPNOTSUPP and report 0 bytes sent.

problem_statement_fixed: The socket API has no helper that reliably transmits an entire buffer to a connected stream (TCP) peer. zsock_send()/zsock_sendmsg() may return after transferring only part of the data, forcing callers to loop themselves. Add two public helpers, declared in zephyr/net/socket.h, named zsock_send_all and zsock_sendmsg_all. Their required prototypes are: int zsock_send_all(int sock, const void *buf, size_t len, int flags, k_timeout_t timeout, size_t *sent_len); int zsock_sendmsg_all(int sock, const struct net_msghdr *msg, int flags, k_timeout_t timeout, size_t *sent_len); The first helper takes a plain buffer, the second takes a net_msghdr. Each helper must send all requested data and block, up to the caller-supplied timeout, until everything is sent or an error/timeout occurs. Each helper reports the number of bytes actually sent through the output pointer (which may be NULL); if the pointer is non-NULL it is reset to 0 by the helper. The helpers return 0 on full success, -ETIMEDOUT if the timeout elapses, and -errno on other failures. The helpers are only valid for stream sockets; calling them on a non-stream socket (e.g. UDP) must fail with -EOPNOTSUPP and report 0 bytes sent.
